hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive gain).
Response lags command by tens of seconds and settles over several minutes, not instantly.
There is negligible dead-zone: u=0.2-0.5 produces a clear rise from current y.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient low values.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across input levels.
Steady-state input needed to hold target y=0.5 is in mid-range ~0.4-0.6.
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) relative to control band width 0.05.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in response direction, magnitude/gain and lag at mid-power, which is required to estimate steady-state input for target and to choose controller gain and timing.
proposal.safety_argument: Starting from y=0.2482, worst-case bound is 0.2482+0.006*0.5*180=0.7882 which is below soft limit 0.85 with margin, and well below hard cutoff 0.9; actual rise will be lower due to heat loss and lag.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y should start near 0.25, rise after a short lag with positive slope, reaching roughly 0.4-0.6 by end of 180s with slope flattening if approaching equilibrium.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero completed experiments so no uncertainties are resolved; gain, lag, zero-decay, linearity, steady-state for target, and noise all remain unmeasured and controller cannot be justified.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: hold mid-power 0.5 for 180 s to measure direction, rate and lag.

proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain linear hypothesis with tau ~150-200s is right, y should rise from ~0.18 after short lag at ~0.001-0.002/s, reaching ~0.40-0.50 by end of 300s with slope declining as it approaches equilibrium near 0.5; flat response would indicate dead-zone, overshoot past 0.6 would indicate larger gain.

proposal.operator_note: Holding at 0.35 power for 300 s from cold to check power needed for target.

proposal.operator_note: Holding just below current power to see if temperature settles inside the target band.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive gain).
Response lags command and settles over several minutes (tau ~150-250s, settle ~300-450s), not instantly.
There is no dead-zone in tested 0.28-0.5 range: u>=0.28 produces clear heating/hold; behavior below u=0.2 is untested.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient ~0.15-0.20.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across all input levels globally.
Steady-state input needed to hold target y=0.5 is ~0.27-0.29; u=0.28 holds ~0.506 in-band, u=0.30 holds ~0.531 just above band, u=0.35 holds >0.55.
Sensor noise is ~0.01-0.02 RMS with occasional 0.03-0.05 outliers, comparable to band half-width 0.025, not <0.01.
Change is weaker actuator: same u gives smaller heating rise and lower held level, but u=0 cooling rate/delay/ambient and sensor calibration/noise are unchanged from E3/E6-E7.
Change is faster outflow/heat loss: fall at u=0 is faster/steeper than E3 and same u holds lower level, with similar delay and sensor behaviour.
Change is slower response: transport delay is much longer than ~20s and/or heating/cooling time constant is much longer, while steady-state gain and sensor are unchanged.
Change is sensor shift: true thermal dynamics/gain are unchanged but reading has new offset and/or changed noise, so apparent 0.45 level at u~0.30-0.42 does not reflect true temperature.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in post-change delay, u=0 cooling rate/ambient, and sensor offset/noise, which discriminates weaker actuator (same cooling as E3) vs faster outflow (faster fall) vs slower response (longer flat/slower fall) vs sensor (shifted ambient/changed noise) and sets timing and feedforward for revised control.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case rise is current y + RATE*u*duration = 0.4582 + 0.006*0*480 = 0.4582, well below soft limit 0.85; u=0 cannot rise and is safe at any duration.
proposal.expected_observation: If baseline delay/cooling unchanged (weaker-actuator leading case), y should hold ~0.45-0.48 for ~15-25 s after switch (still responding to prior ~0.42 in-transit command), then fall with E3-like slope toward ~0.20-0.25 by end of 480 s; much faster/steeper fall implies faster outflow, much longer flat (>50 s) or much slower fall implies slower response/delay increase, same shape but shifted ambient/noise change implies sensor offset/noise change.
proposal.readiness_justification: Not ready: monitoring shows same u now holds ~0.05-0.08 lower with flat response to +0.12 u ramp, consistent with C1/C2/C3 and partly C4, but with zero after-change experiments delay, cooling slope, ambient, and noise shift are unresolved; one draining hold is needed before designing controller.
proposal.operator_note: Draining at u=0 from 0.46 to measure delay and cooling rate to separate gain, loss, lag, and sensor changes.

proposal.operator_note: Holding 0.35 from low level to compare heating slope and plateau to E4.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Distinguishes weaker actuator (proportionally smaller initial slope at higher u) from faster outflow (near-baseline initial slope then early flatten) and quantifies new gain/feedforward for y=0.5 to set revised controller.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case conservative rise 0.3696 + 0.006*0.6*120 = 0.8016 stays below 0.85 soft limit with no decay/lag assumed, starting from low 0.37; 120s at 0.6 cannot reach soft limit even if gain were baseline.
proposal.expected_observation: If weaker-actuator C1 is right, y should hold ~0.37 for ~15-20s delay then rise at ~0.0006-0.0009/s (about 60% of baseline E1/E4 slope) to ~0.41 by +60s and ~0.44-0.47 by 120s still rising; if faster-outflow C2 were right, rise would start at near-baseline ~0.0012-0.0015/s to ~0.44 by +60s then flatten early toward <0.48 by 120s; flat >50s would revive slow-response C3.
proposal.readiness_justification: Delay (~15-20s, E8 immediate fall, E9 rise in ~20s), u=0 cooling/ambient similarity (E8 normalized k similar to E3), and unchanged noise are resolved enough to reject slow-response and sensor-shift, but gain magnitude/new feedforward for 0.5 remains uncertain (C1 vs C2, C5 wide), so one high-u slope test is needed before controller design.
proposal.operator_note: Probing high-power heating slope from current low level to separate weaker heater from faster loss and estimate new feedforward.
